summary:
Plan of w135 (supervision#r67, intake round) written as far as it goes, in .shop/scratch/2-plan/plan.md.
Both examples are red at the unbound first Given. `work run` with no initiative is a usage error, and no code or agent job does intake.
Decisions: select open/awaiting-upstream upstream requests; the round writes through `work outcome`/`work turn` itself (r67 note, decision 0067), with an intake Bash list; a question on a line is written as a non-settled outcome (requests#r17).
The session is an initiative-round in its own worktree. Its commits of q1 alone are brought onto the checked-out branch and pushed. Any other .shop/work change is a fault.
A fault exits with an error naming the request, and nothing is brought over.
New module scripts/supervise_intake.py plus a CLAUDE.md row, and new steps module tests/scenarios/supervision_intake_steps.py.
Tests broken: none (verified from notes part 4 and the tool-list and agent tests).
Q1: wait on w134's no-initiative path, or add the entry in w135. Q2: does `work run <initiative>` also start intake rounds.
questions: Does w135 wait on w134 for `work run` with no initiative? The r67 outline's When is `work run` with no initiative (supervision#r66, accepted by w134, which is researched and blocked_by w146 and w136, both drafted). w135 is blocked_by w127 only. Reading A: w135 gets blocked_by [work-item/w134] and builds on w134's no-initiative driver. The narrator sees no intake round from any `work run` until w146, w136, w134 and then w135 are green. Reading B: w135 makes `work run`'s initiative optional and, when none is given, runs only the intake pass, exiting successfully unless a round faults. w134 later adds the initiatives' pass. The narrator sees `work run` take in upstream requests as soon as w135 is merged, and until w134 is green that run takes no initiative.

Does `work run <initiative>` also start intake rounds? r67's trigger is the request's state and does not say which `work run`. The Purpose says `work run <initiative>` takes 'that initiative'. Reading A: every `work run`, with or without an initiative, first gives each open or awaiting-upstream upstream request to an intake round. The narrator running `work run i1` with q1 open sees an intake round of q1, with q1's outcomes committed on i1's branch. Reading B: only `work run` with no initiative starts intake rounds. The narrator running `work run i1` sees q1 untouched, and q1 is taken in only by a `work run` with no initiative.
